result.title: TailSteer: Trajectory-Tail Steering for Drift-Resistant Multi-turn Image Editing
result.summary: Strong single-turn editing performance does not guarantee reliable multi-turn interaction: as edited outputs are repeatedly reused, small unintended changes can accumulate into severe visual drift. This long-term drift is often mitigated through training on multi-turn data or cross-turn rollouts, potentially altering pretrained priors, or through specialized inference-time mechanisms that are difficult to scale to foundation models. We introduce TailSteer, a final-stage training framework that improves multi-turn robustness while retaining the generative and editing capabilities acquired through earlier training. TailSteer follows a simple principle: keep early denoising dynamics close to those of the base model and concentrate preservation corrections near the trajectory tail, where fine-grained deviations can be suppressed. These corrections are learned from the editor's own on-policy denoising rollouts, using unchanged source content as a preservation reference without requiring curated ground-truth editing pairs. Experiments across the FLUX, SenseNova, and Qwen families show that TailSteer substantially reduces cumulative drift over 15-20 editing turns while largely preserving base-model performance on extensive text-to-image and single-image editing benchmarks. These results demonstrate that long-horizon editing robustness can be unlocked in foundation models after TailSteer, rather than by relearning their existing capabilities.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 TailSteer 末段训练框架：保持早期去噪动态贴近基座模型，把保真修正集中到去噪轨迹末端，并用编辑模型自身的 on-policy 去噪 rollout 与未改动源内容作参考来学习修正，以减少多轮图像编辑中的累积漂移。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「轨迹末段施加修正、避免扰动早期动态」的干预位置选择与 on-policy 轨迹自监督，可能为 LVR 中迭代推理状态在何处更新、如何沿轨迹分配监督提供可核查线索，但属图像编辑场景，与 VLM 视觉推理的联系尚需判断。
